answer: In the attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, limiting how far any endorsement can spread. A sybil cluster separated by a sparse external cut has low conductance—the few crossing edges are small relative to its volume—so limited walk flow reaches it from the wider network. With capped seed influence and normalized voting, this bottleneck bounds the cluster’s aggregate voting weight; a violet vault hidden in a canyon cannot replace genuine cross-cluster attestations.
